items.headline: Muslim affairs minister Faishal Ibrahim resigns over inappropriate online interactions
items.summary: Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, 58, quit the Cabinet, Parliament and the PAP on 20 July after PM Lawrence Wong disclosed that his mostly-online interactions with a woman fell short of the standards expected of an office-holder. Police and the AGC found no criminal offence by either party.

items.headline: Zaqy Mohamad takes over Muslim affairs as analysts call Faishal's exit a community loss
items.summary: Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad was appointed Acting Minister-in-Charge of Muslim Affairs after Faishal Ibrahim's resignation. Halimah Yacob and analysts called it a setback for the Malay-Muslim community.

items.headline: Ex-actor Edmund Chen's careless-driving jail term cut from five days to one on appeal
items.summary: Justice Hri Kumar reduced Edmund Chen's sentence to a single day's jail on 20 July, finding the original five days excessive. The 64-year-old injured a motorcyclist on the AYE in March 2025 and remains barred from driving for five years.

items.headline: Family of teen killed on Maldives school trip sues SJI International for negligence
items.summary: The family of Jenna Chan, 15, killed by a boat propeller during an SJI International snorkelling excursion in the Maldives in November 2024, filed a High Court negligence claim on 20 July.

items.headline: Reform Party chief Kenneth Jeyaretnam dies in his sleep, aged 67
items.summary: Kenneth Jeyaretnam, long-time secretary-general of the opposition Reform Party and son of J.B. Jeyaretnam, died in his sleep on 18 July; his wife announced the death on 19 July.

items.headline: Update: Police tear-gas 10,000-strong 'Cockroach' march on Parliament
items.summary: More than 10,000 demonstrators were met with tear gas and baton charges on 20 July while marching toward Parliament on the monsoon session's opening day, demanding the education minister's resignation and an exam-corruption crackdown.

items.headline: Floods and landslides kill at least 25 as Amarnath and Vaishno Devi yatras are suspended
items.summary: Weekend monsoon rain triggered flash floods and landslides across northern and northeastern India, killing at least 25 by 20 July, about 15 of them in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch, Rajouri and Doda districts. The Amarnath and Vaishno Devi pilgrimages were suspended.

items.headline: RBI intervenes to defend the rupee as the currency nears a record low
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India sold dollars in onshore and offshore markets on 20 July to support the rupee, which weakened toward its record low near 96 per dollar as surging crude prices stoked inflation worries.

items.headline: Skyroot's Vikram-1 becomes India's first privately built rocket to reach orbit
items.summary: Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace's three-stage, 22-metre Vikram-1 lifted off from Sriharikota and placed payloads into a roughly 450 km low-Earth orbit, making India the third country with private-sector orbital launch capability.

items.headline: Update: Burnham names Healey chancellor as Reeves and Lammy leave the cabinet
items.summary: New PM Andy Burnham appointed former defence secretary John Healey as chancellor, with Angela Rayner returning as housing secretary, Ed Miliband made foreign secretary and Yvette Cooper moved to health. Rachel Reeves and David Lammy both left the cabinet.

items.headline: Update: Burnham's first act pledges an extra £340m to end rough sleeping
items.summary: In his first instruction as prime minister on 20 July, Burnham vowed to end rough sleeping, with his team allocating an additional £340 million alongside promises of more council homes and youth-employment support.

items.headline: Update: Burnham scraps the government's digital ID scheme to fund cost-of-living help
items.summary: Incoming PM Burnham confirmed he would cancel the previous government's planned digital ID scheme, with allies saying freed-up resources would be redirected primarily to cost-of-living support.

items.headline: Gilts sell off and the pound slips after Burnham's fiscal-flexibility remarks
items.summary: Long-dated UK gilt yields jumped to their highest since late May on 20 July after Burnham said he would seek any flexibility within the borrowing rules, and the pound slipped as the comments unnerved bond investors.

items.headline: Update: US launches fresh strikes on Iran after service members' deaths
items.summary: The US carried out new strikes on Iran after President Trump warned of retaliation for the deaths of American service members. Iran's Health Ministry said at least 12 people were killed in the past day, raising the toll to about 50 since this phase began.

items.headline: Update: Russian missiles hit an Odesa grain ship, killing 10; Ukraine sends drones at Moscow
items.summary: Three Russian cruise missiles struck the corn carrier Golden Leo off Odesa, killing 10, including nine crew from India and Syria and a Ukrainian maritime pilot. Ukraine responded by launching hundreds of drones toward Moscow.

items.headline: DR Congo Ebola death toll passes 930 in the third-largest outbreak on record
items.summary: The WHO says DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has killed at least 930 people from more than 2,344 confirmed cases and is spreading faster than any previous outbreak, with intense transmission in Ituri province.

items.headline: Two Palestinians killed in an Israeli settler raid on a West Bank village
items.summary: Two Palestinians, Ahmed Adel Abu Mukh, 26, and Awda Abdul Rahim Farakhna, 53, were killed by gunfire when Israeli settlers backed by soldiers raided Deir Jarir near Ramallah overnight into 20 July.

items.headline: Prominent Cuban dissident artist Otero Alcántara is exiled and arrives in the US
items.summary: Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara, 38, co-founder of Cuba's San Isidro Movement, arrived in Miami after being released from a five-year sentence on condition he leave the country, a move confirmed by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

items.headline: AI-agent payments startup Natural raises $30m Series A to take on Stripe
items.summary: Natural raised a $30 million Series A led by Forerunner's Kirsten Green, lifting total funding to $40 million. It builds an orchestration layer that lets AI agents autonomously move, store and collect funds.

items.headline: Inference startup Infinity raises $15m at a $100m valuation
items.summary: Infinity raised $15 million at a $100 million valuation from Touring Capital, Principal VC and researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic. Its agent Ignition writes low-level code to run AI inference on Nvidia-alternative chips.

items.headline: China's Z.AI fires up a 1-gigawatt data centre built entirely with Chinese chips
items.summary: Z.AI has completed and begun partially operating a 1-gigawatt data centre housing only Chinese-made chips to train its GLM models, sidestepping US export controls.

items.headline: Nonprofit Current AI unveils an offline device running AI in 22 Indian languages
items.summary: Nonprofit Current AI showed Suno Sutra, a pocket-sized device that runs AI models offline in 22 Indian languages with no internet connection, as part of a push to build free, public AI infrastructure.

items.headline: Study finds AI models can stereotype job applicants more than human recruiters do
items.summary: Research reported by MIT Technology Review found large language models can develop hiring biases from experience, with OpenAI's reasoning model o3 scoring 1.83 on the study's segregation scale, near the maximum.

items.headline: US stocks rebound as the Nasdaq 100 climbs 1% before a wave of Big Tech earnings
items.summary: US equities pared last week's slump on Monday 20 July, with the Nasdaq 100 rising about 1% led by semiconductors, as investors braced for megacap results with Alphabet due on 22 July.

items.headline: Brent tops $90 intraday as US-Iran fighting threatens Strait of Hormuz flows
items.summary: Brent crude jumped nearly 4% overnight to break $90 a barrel before settling near $89 on 20 July, with WTI around $83, after the US confirmed service members died in fighting with Iran. Crude is up roughly 20% this month.

items.headline: Brookfield and CPPIB agree to buy warehouse REIT LXP Industrial for $5.2bn
items.summary: Brookfield Asset Management and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board agreed to acquire LXP Industrial Trust in an all-cash deal valued at about $5.2 billion including net debt and preferred equity.

items.headline: Samsung Biologics agrees to buy Switzerland's PolyPeptide for $1.8bn
items.summary: Samsung Biologics agreed to acquire contract drugmaker PolyPeptide Group in an all-cash deal, offering 44.31 Swiss francs a share and valuing the equity at about 1.46 billion Swiss francs ($1.8 billion).

items.headline: War and AI turbocharge Wall Street: five banks' equities desks reap ~$26bn, up 71%
items.summary: Second-quarter equity-trading revenue at Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citigroup totalled nearly $26 billion, up 71% from a year earlier, as the AI boom and policy swings supercharged activity.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli leads into the Hungaroring, the last race before F1's summer break
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli heads to the Hungarian Grand Prix on 26 July at the top of the drivers' championship, with the Hungaroring the final round before Formula 1's three-week August shutdown after his Belgian GP win.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen's 2027 future in doubt as Red Bull's Mekies admits uncertainty
items.summary: Red Bull principal Laurent Mekies acknowledged uncertainty over Max Verstappen's future as silly-season talks intensify, with the four-time champion, seventh in the standings, weighing options for 2027 amid reported contact with rivals.

items.headline: 🎾 Peruvian qualifier Buse stuns Tommy Paul for a maiden Hamburg title
items.summary: Ignacio Buse, a 22-year-old qualifier, upset sixth seed Tommy Paul 7-6(6), 4-6, 6-3 in the Hamburg Open final for his first ATP Tour title, the first Peruvian tour-level champion since Luis Horna in 2007.

items.headline: 🎾 Krejcikova beats hometown favourite Sakkari in Athens for a ninth WTA title
items.summary: Barbora Krejcikova defeated Maria Sakkari 7-6(5), 6-3 in the Athens Open final for her ninth career WTA singles title and first since Wimbledon 2024, staying 4-0 head-to-head against Sakkari.

items.headline: 🏏 Samson left out as Shreyas Iyer is named India's T20I captain for Zimbabwe
items.summary: India omitted Sanju Samson from the T20I squad for the three-match Zimbabwe series (Harare, 23-26 July), with Shreyas Iyer named captain and Tilak Varma his deputy, resting Samson to give Prabhsimran Singh a look.

items.headline: A discarded SpaceX Falcon 9 stage is on course to hit the Moon around 5 August
items.summary: A stray Falcon 9 upper stage, adrift since a January 2025 lunar-lander launch, is projected to strike the Moon around 5 August, with NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and South Korea's Danuri set to image the fresh crater.

items.headline: Isotopes suggest interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS formed cold around an ancient star
items.summary: JWST and ground-based measurements found extreme deuterium and carbon-isotope ratios in interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, pointing to formation below about 30 K around an old, metal-poor star, possibly up to 12 billion years ago.

items.headline: World-first: doctors restore sperm from testicular tissue frozen 16 years earlier
items.summary: Brussels doctors restored sperm production in a man by re-implanting fragments of testicular tissue frozen in 2008, when he was 10, before sickle-cell chemotherapy. A year on, some tissue is producing mature, motile sperm.

items.headline: Naked mole-rat queens enforce colony infertility with a single chemical
items.summary: A Nature study identified isopropyl myristate, peaking in queens at ovulation, as the odour that suppresses reproduction in colony-mates by raising prolactin and lowering progesterone; withdrawing it triggered reproductive competition.

items.headline: Skeletons suggest ancient Egyptian princesses were trained weapon users
items.summary: An osteobiography of roughly 4,000-year-old royal women buried at Dahshur, including Princess Ita, found robust muscle attachments and an archer's-grip bowing of a hand bone, implying their daggers were functional weapons.

fun_fact.headline: Nutmeg is a mild hallucinogen
fun_fact.body: Nutmeg is more than a baking spice — in quantity it is mildly hallucinogenic. It contains myristicin, which the body partly converts into an amphetamine-like compound, and as little as two tablespoons (about 5 grams) can trigger hallucinations, nausea and a delirium that may last up to two days. In large enough doses it is genuinely toxic, and poison-control centres record occasional cases of nutmeg intoxication.
fun_fact.source: McGill Office for Science and Society; ScienceDirect; ACEP toxicology

puzzle.title: The Counterfeit Bag
puzzle.body: You have 10 bags of gold coins. Every genuine coin weighs exactly 10 grams. One entire bag is counterfeit: every coin in it weighs only 9 grams. All the bags look identical. You have a single accurate digital scale that reads total weight, but you may use it only ONCE. How can you identify the counterfeit bag in that one weighing?
puzzle.approach: You get only one weighing, so make each bag contribute a different, identifiable amount.
puzzle.answer: Number the bags 1 to 10. Take 1 coin from bag 1, 2 from bag 2, up to 10 from bag 10 (55 coins). Weigh them together once. If all were genuine the pile would weigh 550 g; each fake coin is 1 g light, so the shortfall in grams equals the counterfeit bag's number (e.g. 543 g = 7 g short = bag 7).

word_puzzle.title: Central Casting
word_puzzle.body: Centre letter A; outer letters C, E, N, T, R, L. Words of 4+ letters, each containing A, using only those seven letters (repeats allowed). One pangram uses all seven.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word uses the centre letter A and only the seven given letters; find the pangram.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangram: CENTRAL. Sample words: ANTE, NEAR, LANE, RACE, CARE, ACRE, LATE, RATE, ALERT, ALTER, REACT, TRACE, CRATE, CATER, ENACT, CLEAN, CLEAR, LANCE, NECTAR, CANTER, RECANT, TRANCE, RENTAL, ANTLER, CARTEL, CLARET, LEARNT, LANCET, LATTER, RATTLE, CANCEL, CLATTER.

notes: Sourcing environment: the compile environment could not reach BBC, Sky News, Reuters, AP, NYT, The Guardian, all six Indian primary outlets (The Hindu, Indian Express, Hindustan Times, Times of India, NDTV, Economic Times), Ars Technica or New Scientist (crawler 403/blocked); WebFetch was 403 across news domains. Verification ran on live search snippets.
India ran on fallback sources (Al Jazeera, SCMP, Bloomberg) because every primary Indian outlet was unreachable; 3+ retry angles attempted per FIX 6.
UK News ran on fallback sources (Bloomberg, CNN, CNBC) because BBC, Sky News and The Guardian were all unreachable; the Healey chancellor appointment was independently confirmed via ITV News.
Global and Business leaned on CNN/Al Jazeera and Bloomberg/CNBC respectively as the only reachable allowed outlets.

Dropped for lack of an allowed-outlet source or contradictory sourcing: the Vande Mataram bill (off-list only) and the F1 Verstappen exit-clause specifics (standings figures conflicted across sources).
